property_summary: After cancelProposal, the proposalCount should be the maximum proposal ID used in any mapping (i.e., the highest index among all stored proposals).
The proposalCount should not decrease after a new proposal and cancelProposal.

After cancelProposal(oldProposalID, newProposalID), the value of proposalCount equals oldProposalID (since newGrantProposal only increments proposalCount twice, making the last created proposal have an odd ID, and cancelProposal does not change proposalCount).

After cancelProposal(old, new), the proposalCount value modulo 2 is 0, because in the reference it is always incremented exactly once per proposal, making odd IDs correspond to proposals, while in the buggy version it is incremented twice, making the count equal to 2*proposalCount + 1 (odd).
After cancelProposal(old, new), the value of proposalCount is consistent with the number of proposals having been incremented once per newGrantProposal call.
The number of proposals that have been created (by any proposal-creating function) is exactly proposalCount, because each newGrantProposal call increments it once.
The proposalCount after cancelProposal is congruent to the number of newGrantProposal calls modulo 2.

After any series of public actions ending in cancelProposal, the proposalCount before and after cancelProposal must be consistent with the fact that cancelProposal only resets votes without incrementing proposalCount.
After cancelProposal, the proposalCount must be strictly less than the sum of the two proposal IDs used as arguments.
After cancelProposal, proposalCount must equal the maximum of the two proposal IDs that were provided as arguments, because cancelProposal does not change proposalCount.
After cancelProposal, the proposalCount must equal the value it had before the call, because cancelProposal only resets votes without incrementing.

After any series of public actions ending in cancelProposal, the proposalCount must equal the maximum of the two proposal IDs provided as arguments, because cancelProposal does not change proposalCount.

The number of proposals (proposalCount) is equal to the maximum proposal ID that has been assigned via newGrantProposal or newAddressProposal, which in this case should never decrease after a cancelProposal call.
After cancelProposal(old, new), the proposalCount must be at least as large as the old proposal ID.
After cancelProposal is called with valid parameters, the proposalCount must be at least as large as the max(oldProposalID, newProposalID).
After cancelProposal(old, new), proposalCount is at least as large as the maximum proposal ID ever created (using maxID), which must be >= the old proposalID.
The proposalCount must never decrease after a successful cancelProposal call.
After cancelProposal, proposalCount never decreases.

After any sequence of public actions ending with cancelProposal, the total number of proposals created (including both grant and address proposals) is at least as large as the number of distinct proposal IDs ever assigned to address proposals.
After cancelProposal, the total number of proposals (proposalCount) is at least the maximum proposal ID ever assigned to an address proposal.
After any call to cancelProposal, the VADER address must remain unchanged from its initial value set in init.
After any call to cancelProposal, the VADER address must be exactly 1 wei less than the originally set value from init.
After cancelProposal is called on a proposal of type 'UTILS' or 'REWARD' that has been finalised, the VADER address must be the proposed address from that proposal.
After any call to cancelProposal with non-finalising proposals, the VADER address equals the initially set VADER address from init.
After any sequence of operations ending with cancelProposal, the VADER address is never set to the hardcoded value 0x123...890.
After a cancelProposal call, the USDV address must equal the initial _usdv parameter passed to init, not the zero address.
After cancelProposal, USDV equals the second argument of init() (the original _usdv parameter), not the first argument.

After cancelProposal always reverts for proposals of type 'GRANT' when USDV was incorrectly set to VADER, because the subsequent call to grantFunds will fail due to insufficient allowance or balance check (USDV is not the actual stablecoin).
The USDV address must remain the vault's address after cancelProposal, unless the cancelProposal call modifies USDV.
After cancelProposal, the USDV address stored in the contract is unchanged from its initial value set during init.
After any sequence of calls ending with cancelProposal, the USDV address is never zero.
The USDV address remains unchanged after any cancelProposal call.

After a cancelProposal call that succeeds, the USDV value is equal to the _usdv argument passed in init when cancelProposal's arguments are different proposal IDs and the old proposal is finalising and the new proposal has minority.
After any cancelProposal call, USDV retains its value set during init.
After any sequence of calls ending with cancelProposal, USDV is always equal to the original _usdv argument passed in init.
